title: NAHB/Wells Fargo Housing Market Index (December 2026) — the residential read a funding lapse cannot stop, 10:00 a.m. ET
source: EST: nahb.org/news-and-economics/housing-economics/indices/nahb-wells-fargo-housing-market-index-release-dates fetched direct 2026-09-06 (HTTP 200, 47,132 bytes) — the publisher's own "2026 HMI Schedule" table, standing note "Normal release time: 10:00 AM Eastern Time", row "Dec. 2026 | December, 16, 2026" (the stray comma is NAHB's, transcribed verbatim rather than silently corrected). The same table's 78 already-elapsed 2026-and-prior rows are internally consistent with the mid-month Mon/Tue convention across seven archived years, and Wednesday 2026-12-16 is a normal trading session. Filed `estimate` per this lane's no-self-confirm limit on an event discovered in-sweep, not because the source is weak — the sibling nahb-hmi-2026-11-17.json carries `IR:`/`confirmed` off this same table, and that precedent is available to whichever lane researches this id. Checked 2026-09-06
notes: DISCOVERED during the nahb-hmi-2026-11-17 initial-research adjacency sweep (2026-09-06), from the publisher's own 2026 schedule. Why it earns its own row rather than a line in that ledger: it is the ONE residential release in the post-cliff corridor with no funding exposure. The housing-starts-2026-11-18 and -12-17 ledgers measured that all 9 out-of-month slips in the Census series' 514 release dates since 1984 are funding-lapse slips, that the 2025-26 lapse cost 114 dark days, and that 2026-12-17 sits 6 days after cr-expiry-2026-12-11 (`estimate`, `high`). This print lands 12-16, 5 days after that cliff and one session BEFORE the exposed Census print — and NAHB is a private trade association, so no appropriations lapse reaches it. If the cliff bites, this is the residential datapoint that still publishes when 12-17 does not. Two structural facts carried forward from the proposing lane's own measurement so they are not re-derived: the HMI is the trading day immediately before New Residential Construction 91.0% of the time (71 of 78 days, 2020-01-16 -> 2026-08-17), and 12-16/12-17 is another instance; and 2026-12-16 is already the corridor's stacked morning — retail-sales-2026-12-16, industrial-production-2026-12-16 and mtis-2026-12-16 all share the date, the same 08:30/09:15/10:00 pile-up as 2026-11-17. What that lane already settled, so this one need not re-litigate it: the builder-SENTIMENT channel is measured null (ITB open->close on the 78 HMI days 0.9559% vs 0.9627% baseline, p=0.96; the paired sentiment-vs-data test on 71 consecutive-session pairs is 35/71 = 49.3%, sign test p=1.00), and the pre-open lift on a stacked HMI morning belongs to the 09:15 G.17 release, not the 10:00 HMI (HMI+G.17 SPY gap 0.4828% vs 0.3275% clean baseline, p=0.0385; HMI-only 0.3391%, p=0.85). So the open question this id actually carries is NOT the tape — it is whether a private residential print acquires information value precisely when the federal ones go dark, which nobody here has measured and which only a realized lapse can test. Proposed as an estimate; nothing here licenses an entry.
